title: OSHA Foot Protection Checklist (29 CFR 1910.136)
subtitle: Use during area walk-throughs and when checking footwear issued to employees in foot-hazard areas.
instructions: Mark every item OK, Defect or N/A.
For any Defect, record what was found, correct it (for example, supply compliant footwear) before the employee works in the hazard area again, and note the date it was fixed.
The footwear manufacturer's instructions and your site rules may add checks, such as condition and replacement of worn footwear.

sections.title: Hazard areas and footwear use
items: Every employee working where objects could fall on the feet is wearing protective footwear.
Every employee working where objects could roll onto or over the feet is wearing protective footwear.
Every employee working where objects could pierce the sole is wearing protective footwear.
Where footwear protects against a static-discharge or electric-shock hazard, affected employees are wearing footwear suited to that hazard.
The other necessary protective measures for the electrical hazard are in place, and footwear addresses only the hazard that remains.
Supervisors confirm that each affected employee in these areas is actually wearing the footwear, not just issued it.

sections.title: Footwear criteria
items: Manufacturer marking or documentation shows the footwear meets ASTM F-2412-2005 and ASTM F-2413-2005.
Manufacturer marking or documentation shows the footwear meets ANSI Z41-1999.
Manufacturer marking or documentation shows the footwear meets ANSI Z41-1991.
Footwear not built to a listed standard
The employer can demonstrate the footwear is at least as effective as footwear constructed to one of the listed standards.

references: 29 CFR 1910.136: Foot protection (Part 1910 Subpart I, Personal Protective Equipment)
Source: eCFR, Title 29, text as of 2026-11-09
